x: Bert is now 31st, our friend Bert Cook is observed 42nd, Warboys 63rd, Allum 77th, Bill Webb 90th, Duffett, 108th, and Frank Webb down to 110.
The two-miles saw Bert Cook, after being behind for the greater part of the race, take the lead in the last 200 yards and gallop away with Arthur Allum in close attendance.

A large field turned out for the 2 miles run with Bert Cook on the post of honour. He was conceding Allum and Jack Flower 5yds., but once the pistol went these two jumped away from him and commenced to forge their way through the field.
Bert Cook recorded his fastest time for some while to take second place; and third prize was claimed by A.
Syd Ring and Bert Cook were on the virtual scratch mark of one minute and to Ring falls the honour of doing the fastest time, viz., 29 min. 41 sec.
In fact, we had the first ten home, but as Bert Cook is only a second-claim member, he was eliminated from the scoring, and we had our 10 in 12.
Next for us came Syd Ring, striving to put every second possible between himself and the following men; then Bert Cook, the evergreen; and "Mick" Walker.
Tobin, of Belgrave, off 100, was second and Bert Cook, better known as a Poly Harrier, was third off 110 yards.
